title: Entra ID adds risk-based CAPTCHA before SMS and voice MFA codes (MC1551151)
summary: Per MC1551151 (13 November 2026), Microsoft Entra ID starts showing a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA, provided by Arkose Labs) before it sends an SMS code or places a voice call for MFA, rolling out worldwide from mid-November 2026. It extends the same safeguard that has applied to SMS/voice first-factor sign-in since mid-October (MC1518029). Microsoft does not publish the risk criteria. It is separate from, and does not change, the 1 February 2027 retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice.
why: This is anti-IRSF (toll fraud) hardening, not a phishing control. The operational risk is a hard failure: if a proxy, SWG, DNS filter or TLS inspection blocks Arkose Labs, the challenge does not load and the user cannot get a code at all. Expect help desk tickets that look like 'MFA SMS never arrives' from users behind restrictive egress.
todo: Allow outbound HTTPS 443 to `arkoselabs.com` and `*.arkoselabs.com` on proxies/SWGs (add both; some products do not match the apex with a wildcard), above any category block.
Exclude both domains from TLS inspection, which Microsoft says can stop the challenge from validating.
Brief the service desk: the CAPTCHA is expected, and the fix for 'cannot complete' is network or another method, not resetting MFA.
Use it as another nudge for the passkey migration that the February 2027 retirement already requires.
effective_note: Microsoft says 'beginning in mid-November 2026'; 15 November is an approximation of that, not a published date.
